passages.text: <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression is induced by all-<italic toggle="yes">trans</italic> retinoic acid in P19 cells prior to acquisition of neural fate

TAL2 is a member of the basic helix-loop-helix family and is essential for the normal development of the mouse brain. <sentence_start/>However, the function of TAL2 during brain development is unclear. <sentence_start/>P19 cells are pluripotent mouse embryonal carcinoma cells that adopt neural fates upon exposure to all-<italic toggle="yes">trans</italic> retinoic acid (atRA) and culture in suspension. <sentence_start/>We found that the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene was induced in P19 cells after addition of atRA in suspension culture. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was detected within 3 h after the induction, and had nearly returned to basal levels by 24 h. <sentence_start/>When GFP-tagged TAL2 (GFP-TAL2) was expressed in P19 cells, we observed GFP-TAL2 in the nucleus. <sentence_start/>Moreover, we showed that atRA and retinoic acid receptor α regulated <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression. <sentence_start/>These results demonstrate for the first time that atRA induces <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells, and suggest that TAL2 commits to the acquisition of neural fate in brain development.

TAL2 is a transcription factor belonging to the basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) family<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b1" pmid="15925590" doi="10.1016/j.yexcr.2005.03.015" count="1">1</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b2" pmid="17027923" doi="10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.09.114" count="1">2</citation>. <sentence_start/>The <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene is transcribed in SUP-T3 cells derived from a human T-cell leukemia; these cells harbor the t(7;9)(q34;q32) chromosomal translocation<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b3" pmid="1763056" doi="10.1073/pnas.88.24.11416" pmcid="PMC53146" count="1">3</citation>. <sentence_start/>A translocation between chromosomes 7 and 9 is associated with human T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL)<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b4" pmid="2962650" count="1">4</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b5" pmid="2536065" doi="10.1084/jem.169.2.369" pmcid="PMC2189206" count="1">5</citation>. <sentence_start/>Thus, TAL2 may be an oncogene that is activated as a consequence of the chromosomal translocation in T-ALL<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b6" pmid="12567187" doi="10.1038/ng1092" count="1">6</citation>. <sentence_start/>Moreover, <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> overexpression is confirmed in some lung adenocarcinoma tumor tissues<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b7" pmid="19088038" doi="10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-08-0095" pmcid="PMC2605664" count="1">7</citation> and conversely, <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression is significantly lower in ovarian carcinoma tissue than that in normal tissues<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b8" pmid="23136613" doi="10.3892/etm_00000030" pmcid="PMC3490392" count="1">8</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b9" pmid="21971700" doi="10.3892/or.2011.1483" count="1">9</citation>.

Although aberrant TAL2 expression may be involved in development of some cancers, TAL2 is essential for the normal development of the mouse brain. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> is expressed during embryogenesis, and sites of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression include specific regions of the diencephalon, mesencephalon and metencephalon<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b10" pmid="9931488" doi="10.1016/s0169-328x(98)00323-4" count="1">10</citation>. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic>-null mutant mice are viable at birth and initially appear normal. <sentence_start/>However, they develop signs of runting and die between 13 and 32 days after birth; additionally, they display a prominent hydrocephalus at death<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b11" pmid="11071772" doi="10.1006/dbio.2000.9920" count="1">11</citation>. <sentence_start/>These findings indicate that TAL2 plays a pivotal role in development of the mature central nervous system; nevertheless the function of TAL2 in the development processes remains unclear.

P19 cells are a line of pluripotent mouse embryonal carcinoma (EC) cells derived from a teratocarcinoma that formed following transplantation of a 7.5 day embryo into a testis<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b12" pmid="8507558" count="1">12</citation>. <sentence_start/>P19 cells can be induced to differentiate into derivatives of three germ layers-endoderm, mesoderm, or ectoderm-depending on the inducers and the culture conditions. <sentence_start/>Two different treatments-addition of all-<italic toggle="yes">trans</italic> retinoic acid (atRA) and suspension culture for cell aggregation-are required to induce neural differentiation of P19 cells<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b12" pmid="8507558" count="1">12</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b13" pmid="7110336" doi="10.1038/299165a0" count="1">13</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b14" pmid="6656766" doi="10.1128/mcb.3.12.2271" pmcid="PMC370098" count="1">14</citation>. <sentence_start/>Various genes-including <italic toggle="yes">Neurod</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">Neurog1</italic><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b15" pmid="21559470" doi="10.1371/journal.pone.0019174" pmcid="PMC3084770" count="1">15</citation> and <italic toggle="yes">Fgf8</italic><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b16" pmid="19555770" doi="10.1016/j.cellbi.2009.06.015" count="1">16</citation>-that are implicated in neural development are induced in P19 cells following these treatments and during the subsequent neural differentiation. <sentence_start/>atRA is a biologically active form of vitamin A that functions as the activating ligand for three isotypes of retinoic acid receptor (RAR); these isotypes-α, β, and γ-can each form heterodimers with retinoid X receptors (RXRs)<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b17" pmid="8801176" count="1">17</citation>. <sentence_start/>These receptors transduce atRA signals, belong to the family of nuclear receptors, and induce the transcription of target genes when bound with atRA<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b18" pmid="12401878" doi="10.1194/jlr.r100015-jlr200" count="1">18</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b19" pmid="21618588" doi="10.1002/jcb.23200" count="1">19</citation>. <sentence_start/>atRA plays an important role in early embryonic development and in differentiation of the nervous system including patterning of the brain, specification of neural cell fate, and stimulation of neurite outgrowth<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b20" pmid="1661245" count="1">20</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b21" pmid="17882253" doi="10.1038/nrn2212" count="1">21</citation>. <sentence_start/>Additionally, atRA can induce EC cells, including P19 cells, and embryonic stem cells to adopt neural fates<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b22" pmid="7593279" doi="10.1242/jcs.108.10.3181" count="1">22</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b23" pmid="15717849" doi="10.33549/physiolres.930526" count="1">23</citation>. <sentence_start/>P19 cells have been used as model cells for the studies of neural differentiation, and these studies have led to the discovery of a number of genes that are important for neural development <italic toggle="yes">in vivo</italic><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b12" pmid="8507558" count="1">12</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b24" pmid="8024542" doi="10.1002/bies.950160509" count="1">24</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b25" pmid="12147139" doi="10.1046/j.1432-0436.2002.700409.x" count="1">25</citation>. <sentence_start/>To understand how the neural fate is acquired in early embryonic development, we have attempted to identify genes that commit to the neural fate using P19 cells that were introduced into the neural differentiation. <sentence_start/>In these studies, we found that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was immediately upregulated in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>Here, we investigated the relationship of atRA, cell aggregation, and <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction in P19 cells.
Results
<italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> was transiently expressed in P19 cells introduced into the neural differentiation

We found that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was upregulated in P19 cells introduced into the neural differentiation for our study using DNA microarray experiments (unpublished data). <sentence_start/>To study the alteration of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in more detail here, we extracted RNA from P19 cells 0, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36 and 48 h after addition of atRA in suspension culture, and investigated <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells (Fig. 1a). <sentence_start/>We also examined the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Pou5f1</italic> gene (also known as <italic toggle="yes">Oct3/4</italic>), which encodes the transcription factor in pluripotent cells, and <italic toggle="yes">Ascl1</italic> gene (also known as <italic toggle="yes">Mash1</italic>), which encodes a neurogenic bHLH transcription factor, to assess whether P19 cells were induced to neural cell fate. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Pou5f1</italic> expression decreases during neural differentiation of P19 cells<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b26" pmid="19097998" doi="10.1074/jbc.M807745200" pmcid="PMC3837441" count="1">26</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b27" pmid="23613978" doi="10.1371/journal.pone.0061938" pmcid="PMC3629135" count="1">27</citation>; contemporaneously, <italic toggle="yes">Ascl1</italic> expression increases<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b27" pmid="23613978" doi="10.1371/journal.pone.0061938" pmcid="PMC3629135" count="1">27</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b28" pmid="9352625" doi="10.1620/tjem.182.327" count="1">28</citation>. <sentence_start/>As previously reported, <italic toggle="yes">Pou5f1</italic> expression decreased and <italic toggle="yes">Ascl1</italic> expression increased contemporaneously in atRA-treated, aggregated P19 cells. <sentence_start/>This observation demonstrated that P19 cells lost the pluripotency by addition of atRA in suspension culture and were entered into neural cell fate. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression increased within 3 h after treatment, and <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> mRNA levels was returned to the basal levels within 24 h after treatment. <sentence_start/>In contrast, the expression of all three genes-<italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">Pou5f1</italic>, and <italic toggle="yes">Ascl1</italic>-was not altered by DMSO treatment in suspension culture (see Supplementary Fig. S1 online).

Next, we used real-time PCR assays to measure <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells (Fig. 1b). <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression increased 3 h and 6 h after treatment. <sentence_start/>A reduction in <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression from peak levels was first observed at 12 h and <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was close to the basal levels at 24 h. <sentence_start/>These results indicate that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression is altered in P19 cells for one day.

It has been reported that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was observed in embryonic head (E10.5 to E14.5)<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b10" pmid="9931488" doi="10.1016/s0169-328x(98)00323-4" count="1">10</citation>. <sentence_start/>We also confirmed <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in embryogenesis (Fig. 1c). <sentence_start/>For this purpose, we used a mouse cDNA panel and RT-PCR. <sentence_start/>As previously reported, <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was evident at E11 and was not observed in adult brain. <sentence_start/>In addition, <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> was also hardly observed in E7, E15 and E17. <sentence_start/>The transient expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> was confirmed in mouse embryogenesis, as well as <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> transiently expressed in P19 cells by addition of atRA in suspension culture.
Localization of TAL2 in P19 cells

To examine the behavior of TAL2 in P19 cells, we generated GFP-tagged TAL2 (GFP-TAL2) expression construct. <sentence_start/>This construct was introduced into P19 cells via transfection, and these cells were stained with Hoechst33258 48 h post transfection. <sentence_start/>We then used fluorescence microscopy to visualize these cells (Fig. 2). <sentence_start/>GFP-TAL2 expressed in P19 cells was detected in nuclei.
atRA induced the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene in P19 cells

atRA and cell aggregation are important for neural differentiation of P19 cells<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b12" pmid="8507558" count="1">12</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b13" pmid="7110336" doi="10.1038/299165a0" count="1">13</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b14" pmid="6656766" doi="10.1128/mcb.3.12.2271" pmcid="PMC370098" count="1">14</citation>. <sentence_start/>Thus, we examined how these treatments were involved in the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene. <sentence_start/>When P19 cells were treated with atRA and cultured as a monolayer in culture dishes, <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was nearly the same as that in atRA-treated and cell-aggregated P19 cells (Fig. 3a). <sentence_start/>Additionally, the <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene was not induced by DMSO treatment in suspension culture of P19 cells (see Supplementary Fig. S1 online). <sentence_start/>These results indicate that the induction of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells is associated with atRA.

atRA binds to the RARs (RARα, β, or γ), and RARs form heterodimers with RXRs (RXRα, β, or γ). <sentence_start/>atRA-bound RAR/RXR heterodimer can regulate the transcription of target genes. <sentence_start/>To elucidate the involvement of these receptors in <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction, we confirmed the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Rar</italic> genes and <italic toggle="yes">Rxr</italic> genes in P19 cells after addition of atRA in suspension culture (Fig. 3b). <sentence_start/>For these six genes, the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Rara</italic>, <italic toggle="yes">Rxra</italic> or <italic toggle="yes">Rxrb</italic> was not altered at 48 h. <sentence_start/>The expression of <italic toggle="yes">Rarg</italic> and <italic toggle="yes">Rxrg</italic> had decreased relative to basal levels. <sentence_start/>On the other hand, <italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> expression was not evident at 0 h, but it was evident within 3 h after treatment, as it has been reported that <italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> was induced by retinoic acid in P19 cells<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b29" pmid="2174108" doi="10.1128/mcb.10.12.6445" pmcid="PMC362921" count="1">29</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b30" pmid="1650576" doi="10.1016/0925-4773(91)90025-2" count="1">30</citation>. <sentence_start/>The induction of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> and <italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> were similar in P19 cells, but <italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> expression was not altered from 3 h to 48 h while the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene had decreased from peak levels by 24 h.

Next, in order to investigate the relation between atRA and its receptors, we used four agonists instead of atRA; Am80<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b31" pmid="19531492" doi="10.1074/jbc.M109.026989" pmcid="PMC2755685" count="1">31</citation> (RARα agonist), adapalene<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b32" pmid="9204085" doi="10.1016/s0190-9622(97)70050-1" count="1">32</citation> (RARβ and RARγ agonist), AC-41848 (RARγ agonist) and methoprene acid<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b33" pmid="7597096" doi="10.1073/pnas.92.13.6157" pmcid="PMC41661" count="1">33</citation> (RXR pan-agonist). <sentence_start/>Am80 was able to induce <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene as well as atRA. <sentence_start/>Adapalene also induced <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells, but the induction of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> by adapalene was weaker than that by atRA or Am80. <sentence_start/>In contrast, neither AC-41848 nor methoprene acid induced <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression (Fig. 3c). <sentence_start/>Moreover, We also assessed morphological changes of P19 cells that were treated with atRA, DMSO, or each agonist (Fig. 3d). <sentence_start/>P19 cells formed spherical aggregates called embryoid bodies in the presence of atRA, Am80 or adapalene. <sentence_start/>Whereas, DMSO, AC-41848 or methoprene acid did not formed embryoid bodies.
<italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was induced by RARα

Adapalene formed P19 cells into embryoid bodies, and weakly induced the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> compared with atRA or Am80. <sentence_start/>Moreover, it has been reported that adapalene has stimulated RARα weakly<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b32" pmid="9204085" doi="10.1016/s0190-9622(97)70050-1" count="1">32</citation>. <sentence_start/>Although the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> gene was not observed at 0 h in P19 cells, RARα protein was expressed at 0 h. <sentence_start/>Based on these findings, we assumed that RARα had an intimate involvement in <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction in P19 cells.

We used RNA interference to suppress RARα expression in P19 cells, and examine the involvement of RARα and the induction of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic>. <sentence_start/>The RNAi-mediated suppression of RARα in P19 cells was verified by Western blotting (Fig. 4a). <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression significantly decreased by RARα suppression in P19 cells after addition of atRA in suspension culture (Fig. 4b). <sentence_start/>These results indicate that atRA-RARα complexes induce <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene in P19 cells.
Discussion

P19 EC cells are induced into neural differentiation by addition of atRA in suspension culture<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b13" pmid="7110336" doi="10.1038/299165a0" count="1">13</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b14" pmid="6656766" doi="10.1128/mcb.3.12.2271" pmcid="PMC370098" count="1">14</citation>. <sentence_start/>We explore the molecular mechanisms of the entry into neural differentiation using P19 cells. <sentence_start/>We found that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was altered rapidly and transiently in these cells (Fig. 1a and b). <sentence_start/>Interestingly, the transient expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene was observed at the stage of organogenesis during embryonic development (Fig. 1c). <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in embryonic head was reported previously<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b10" pmid="9931488" doi="10.1016/s0169-328x(98)00323-4" count="1">10</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b11" pmid="11071772" doi="10.1006/dbio.2000.9920" count="1">11</citation>, and TAL2 is inferred to play a role at the early stage of brain development. <sentence_start/>Because P19 cells have been used as model cells for the studies of neural differentiation, a detailed investigation of the molecular mechanisms regulating <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells may be key to understanding the function of TAL2 in brain development.

We investigated the correlation of atRA, cell aggregation and <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>As a result, atRA participated in <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction in P19 cells, but cell aggregation was not necessary for <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> induction (Fig. 3a). <sentence_start/>Next, we examined the involvement of RAR/RXR in the induction of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells (Fig. 3c). <sentence_start/>Am80, a RARα agonist, was able to induce <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>Adapalene also weakly induced <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>Although adapalene is an agonist of RARβ and RARγ, it might also react to RARα in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>Indeed, RARα is less responsive to adapalene than RARβ and RARγ, and RXRα is no responsive to adapalene<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b32" pmid="9204085" doi="10.1016/s0190-9622(97)70050-1" count="1">32</citation>. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">Rarb</italic> gene was not expressed in P19 cells at 0 h, and was induced by atRA as well as <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene. <sentence_start/>Therefore, adapalene is thought to stimulate the RARα signaling weakly and to induce the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells. <sentence_start/>Moreover, RARα knock down by RNA interference suppressed <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in P19 cells (Fig. 4b). <sentence_start/>These results indicate that atRA-RARα complexes induce transcription of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> gene in P19 cells.

The embryoid bodies were formed by the agonists, atRA, Am80 and adapalene, that induced the expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> in P19 cells (Fig. 3d). <sentence_start/>These results raise the possibility that TAL2 is also involved in the formation of embryoid bodies of P19 cells. <sentence_start/>TAL2 induced by these agonists might activate genes such as <italic toggle="yes">Fgf8</italic><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b34" pmid="16641368" doi="10.1091/mbc.E05-11-1087" pmcid="PMC1483041" count="1">34</citation> as a transcription factor that are involved in cell aggregation.

The bHLH family to which TAL2 belongs regulates a variety of biological processes. <sentence_start/>The bHLH usually has two functionally distinct domains-the basic domain and the HLH domain. <sentence_start/>The bHLH proteins form dimers via HLH domains and bind DNA via the basic domains. <sentence_start/>These dimers activate target genes in the nucleus<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b2" pmid="17027923" doi="10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.09.114" count="1">2</citation>. <sentence_start/>Therefore, TAL2, which is a bHLH protein, is probably involved in transcriptional activation of target genes in the nucleus. <sentence_start/>Indeed, the GFP-TAL2 fusion protein that we generated localized to nuclei (Fig. 2). <sentence_start/>Moreover, GFP-TAL2 was highly enriched in a part of each nucleus. <sentence_start/>In zebrafish, TAL2 is expressed in the lateral floor plate of the spinal cord<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b35" pmid="14678833" doi="10.1016/s1567-133x(03)00145-5" count="1">35</citation>. <sentence_start/>The floor plate is an important signal center that specifies neurons and glia cells in the ventral neural tube and guides the trajectory of outgrowing axons. <sentence_start/>TAL2 acts upstream of the <italic toggle="yes">gad67</italic> gene that is the GABA-synthesizing enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase in Kolmer-Agduhr″ (KA″) cells of the lateral floor plate<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b36" pmid="20610488" doi="10.1242/dev.048470" count="1">36</citation>. <sentence_start/>However, it is not clear whether the mammalian spinal cord has KA″ cells, and <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> has not yet been observed in the mouse spinal cord.

atRA is important for embryogenesis and the differentiation of the nervous system, and we demonstrated for the first time that <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression was induced by atRA, which introduced P19 cells into neural differentiation. <sentence_start/>In addition, the transient expression of <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> was observed in organogenesis of development. <sentence_start/>These findings suggest that TAL2 plays a role in acquisition of neural cell fate as a transcription factor in neural differentiation. <sentence_start/>Because the neural differentiation of P19 cells in part mimics the development of the nervous system, P19 cells are useful for studying the molecular mechanism of TAL2 in neural differentiation. <sentence_start/>Further work is underway to clarify the function of TAL2 in neural differentiation using the differentiation system of P19 cells.
Methods
Cell culture and neural differentiation

P19C6, a subclone of P19 mouse embryonic carcinoma cell line, was used in this study<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b37" pmid="11414696" doi="10.1006/bbrc.2001.5089" count="1">37</citation>. <sentence_start/>P19C6 was provided by the RIKEN BRC through the National Bio-Resource Project of the MEXT, Japan. <sentence_start/>P19 cells were cultured in α-MEM (Sigma-Aldrich, MO) supplemented with 10% FBS (Life Technologies, CA) and 2 mM L-glutamine (Kanto Chemical, Japan). <sentence_start/>To induce neural differentitation, these cells were aggregated in a suspension culture dish (SUMILON, Japan) at a seeding density of 2 × 10<sup>5</sup> cell/ml in the presence of 1 μM atRA (Sigma-Aldrich), which was dissolved in DMSO (Sigma-Aldrich)<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b28" pmid="9352625" doi="10.1620/tjem.182.327" count="1">28</citation>. <sentence_start/>DMSO concentration in culture condition was 0.01%. <sentence_start/>To identify the RAR and RXR subtypes, 100 nM Am80 (RARα agonist), 100 nM adapalene (RARβ and RARγ agonist), 100 nM AC-41848 (RARγ agonist), or 100 nM methoprene acid (RXR pan-agonist) were used in place of atRA<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b28" pmid="9352625" doi="10.1620/tjem.182.327" count="1">28</citation><citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b29" pmid="2174108" doi="10.1128/mcb.10.12.6445" pmcid="PMC362921" count="1">29</citation>. <sentence_start/>These agonists were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich.
RT-PCR and real-time PCR

RNeasy Mini Kit (QIAGEN, Germany) was used accoding to the manufacturer's instructions to isolate total RNA from P19 cells. <sentence_start/>RT-PCR was performed as described previously<citation ref-type="bibr" rid="b27" pmid="23613978" doi="10.1371/journal.pone.0061938" pmcid="PMC3629135" count="1">27</citation>. <sentence_start/>In brief, reverse transcription was performed with 1 μg of total RNA and SuperScript III reverse transcriptase (Life Technologies). <sentence_start/>AmpliTaq Gold 360 Master Mix (Life Technologies) and gene specific primer were used for amplification of target genes. <sentence_start/>The list of primers can be found as Supplementary Table S1 online. <sentence_start/>The <italic toggle="yes">Gapdh</italic> gene was used as an internal standard. <sentence_start/>To assess <italic toggle="yes">Tal2</italic> expression in normal mouse embryogenesis, MTC Multiple Tissue cDNA Panels (TAKARA BIO, Japan) were used as templates.
